title: Concourse vs. Kyriba: How the Two Compare in 2026
summary: Concourse vs. Kyriba compared: a modern AI-agent treasury platform versus a legacy enterprise TMS. How they differ on forecasting, automation, cost, and fit.
body_markdown:
Concourse and Kyriba come up in the same conversations because they can both be your treasury system. Kyriba is a legacy enterprise treasury management system that centralizes cash, payments, and risk for an analyst to act on. Concourse is an AI agent platform that connects directly to your banks, ERP, and data warehouse and *runs* the treasury work end to end. The comparison is really about that difference: whether a person drives the workflows, or agents do.


This is a focused, head-to-head look at the two. If you want the wider field, we also compare eight[Kyriba alternatives](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/kyriba-alternatives) in a separate guide.


## The short answer


> Concourse can replace a legacy TMS like Kyriba for most finance teams. It connects directly to your banks, ERP, and data warehouse and runs cash forecasting, variance analysis, collections, and reporting end to end, with every number traceable to source. Kyriba's remaining edge is at the very top of the market, where global multinationals depend on a SWIFT payment factory and in-house banking. Choose Concourse if you want AI to run the treasury work; choose Kyriba if your center of gravity is that heavy enterprise payments layer.

## What Kyriba is best at


Kyriba is one of the most widely deployed enterprise treasury management systems in the world, and it earns that position. For large multinationals running thousands of bank accounts across many entities, it centralizes cash positioning, payments, forecasting, and risk in one governed system. Its bank connectivity is the real moat: deep SWIFT and host-to-host coverage, in-house banking, and payment controls that a global treasury depends on.


That depth is also what you pay for. Third-party pricing trackers put Kyriba implementation and professional-services costs in the[$50,000 to $150,000 range](https://www.itqlick.com/kyriba/pricing) before annual licensing, and enterprise rollouts run higher. Setup is widely described as complex, and connecting every bank can take months. For a large multinational, that is a reasonable trade. For a leaner team, it often means paying for breadth you will never use.


## What Concourse is best at


Concourse is an AI agent platform for corporate finance. It connects to your ERP, data warehouse, billing, and banking data, then runs finance workflows autonomously or on triggers: building and refreshing cash forecasts, running variance and flux analysis, chasing receivables through an AR and collections agent, and producing liquidity and board reporting on a schedule.


The difference from a TMS is the execution model. Concourse does not just surface a cash dashboard for an analyst to interpret. Its agents own the work end to end, and every output traces back to source data and is validated against evals built for your business, which answers finance's biggest objection to AI: whether you can defend the number to an auditor or board. It meets teams where they already work, inside ChatGPT, Claude, Slack, Teams, and email, and exports to Excel, PowerPoint, and Google Sheets. Concourse reports customer results including a 75% reduction in manual work and 20+ hours saved per user per month, is SOC 2 Type II certified, and connects to 100+ systems including NetSuite, QuickBooks, Snowflake, Salesforce, and Stripe.


Because it connects directly to your banks alongside your ERP and data warehouse, Concourse can serve as the treasury system that runs your forecasting, analysis, collections, and reporting, not just a tool that sits beside one. The one place a legacy TMS still leads is heavy payment infrastructure: if you operate a global SWIFT payment factory or in-house banking, you may keep a dedicated payments layer for that. For most teams, Concourse covers the treasury work end to end.


## Head to head, by what actually drives the decision


### Bank connectivity and payments


Concourse connects directly to your banks, ERP, and data warehouse, so it has the data it needs to run cash visibility, forecasting, and analysis as your treasury system. Where a legacy TMS still leads is heavy payment infrastructure: if your core need is a global SWIFT payment factory, host-to-host rails, and in-house banking, Kyriba is purpose-built for that and it is not Concourse's focus. Advantage: Kyriba, for teams whose center of gravity is moving money at global scale.


### Cash forecasting and analysis


Both forecast cash, but differently. Kyriba provides forecasting inside the suite for an analyst to build and maintain. Concourse deploys agents that build, refresh, and explain the forecast automatically, and run the variance analysis behind it, with each figure traceable to source. If the bottleneck is the manual work of producing and defending forecasts, that is the gap Concourse is designed to close. Advantage: Concourse.


### Automation and execution


A TMS centralizes data and presents it; a person still does the work between the data and the decision. Concourse's agents execute that work, from collections outreach to reporting, under human approval. This is the clearest philosophical split between the two. Advantage: Concourse.


### Auditability


Both take controls seriously. Kyriba offers enterprise governance and audit trails as a system of record. Concourse makes every agent output traceable back to the query and source data that produced it, and validates it against evals, so an AI-generated number is as defensible as a hand-built one. Even, either way.


### Cost and time to value


Kyriba is an enterprise purchase with implementation commonly cited in the $50k to $150k range before licensing, and a rollout measured in months. Concourse is lighter to deploy, and each customer is paired with a forward-deployed team that handles the integration, so the setup burden does not land on your finance team. Advantage: Concourse for speed and cost; Kyriba if you specifically need the enterprise TMS footprint.


## Can Concourse replace Kyriba?


For most finance teams, yes. Concourse connects directly to your banks, ERP, and data warehouse and runs the workflows a TMS is bought for: cash visibility, forecasting, variance, collections, and reporting, end to end and with every number traceable. Where a legacy TMS still earns its place is the largest, most payments-heavy global treasuries that depend on a SWIFT payment factory or in-house banking. There, some teams keep that payments layer and run Concourse for the treasury and analytical work on top of it, at least during a transition. But replacing a legacy TMS, rather than merely supplementing it, is increasingly the default. We wrote more about that shift in[how we think about build vs. buy for treasury](https://www.concourse.ai/insights/treasury-build-vs-buy) .


## Which should you choose?


- **Choose Concourse** if you want your treasury system to actually do the work: cash forecasting, variance, collections, and reporting run by AI agents, connected directly to your banks and systems, with every number traceable and audit-ready. For most teams it can replace a legacy TMS outright, without a months-long implementation.
- **Choose Kyriba** if your center of gravity is heavy global payments infrastructure: a SWIFT payment factory, host-to-host rails, and in-house banking at multi-entity scale.
- **Run both** only if you need that heavy payments layer today but want to stop doing forecasting, analysis, and reporting by hand. Keep the payment rails and let Concourse run the treasury work, often as a step toward consolidating onto it.


## Frequently asked questions


### Does Concourse replace Kyriba?


For most teams, yes. Concourse connects directly to your banks, ERP, and data warehouse and runs the treasury workflows end to end, so it can serve as your treasury system rather than sit beside one. The main exception is the largest global treasuries that depend on a SWIFT payment factory or in-house banking; those teams may keep a dedicated payments layer and use Concourse for forecasting, variance, collections, and reporting.


### Is Concourse cheaper than Kyriba?


Generally it is lighter and faster to deploy. Kyriba implementation and professional services are commonly cited in the $50,000 to $150,000 range before licensing. Most vendors, Concourse included, use a scoped, talk-to-sales pricing model, so expect a quote based on your systems and workflows rather than a public list price.


### Can Concourse and Kyriba work together?


Yes, if you want them to. Concourse can read an existing TMS at the line level, so during a transition, or if you keep Kyriba for heavy payments, it runs forecasting, variance, collections, and reporting on top of the data Kyriba centralizes. Many teams start here and later consolidate the treasury work onto Concourse.


### What is the main difference between an AI agent and a TMS?


An AI agent platform like Concourse executes the treasury work itself, building forecasts, running variance analysis, and chasing receivables, while tracing every output back to source. A TMS like Kyriba centralizes cash, payments, and risk and presents it for a person to act on instead. One shows you the cash; the other acts on it.


## The bottom line


Concourse and Kyriba can both be your treasury system, but they represent two eras. Kyriba is the legacy enterprise TMS: deep, but heavy to buy, implement, and run, and it still leaves the analytical work to your team. Concourse connects directly to your banks and systems and runs that work with AI agents, every number traceable and board-ready. For most finance teams it can replace a legacy TMS outright; only the largest, most payments-heavy global treasuries still need the traditional TMS underneath. The real question is less "which TMS" and more whether you want software that shows you cash or software that acts on it.
